memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They said to each other, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them thoroughly." They used brick instead of stone, and tar for mortar. Then they said, "Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves; otherwise we will be scattered over the face of the whole earth." - Gen 11:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the human heart shows itself plainly. "Let us build ourselves a city... so that we may make a name for ourselves." Notice how many times it is about them - their bricks, their city, their tower, their name. God is not mentioned once. This was a monument to human achievement, reaching toward heaven not to meet God but to replace Him.

And notice their fear: "otherwise we will be scattered." God had commanded humanity to fill the earth (Gen 9:1), but they wanted to stay together, secure on their own terms. Their building project was rooted both in pride and in fear - the desire for a great name and the refusal to trust God's plan.

This is the human condition in miniature. We want to make a name for ourselves. We want security we can build with our own hands. We reach for the heavens on our own terms rather than receiving what God gives.

The gospel turns Babel upside down. Where humanity said, "let us make a name for ourselves," God said to Abram in the very next chapter, "I will make your name great" (Gen 12:2). What we grasp for in pride, God gives freely in grace. And Christ, who had the highest name of all, "made himself nothing" and was exalted by the Father, given "the name that is above every name" (Phil 2:7-9). Stop building your tower. Receive your name from God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you trying to make a name for yourself, or receiving your worth from God?
- What "tower" are you building for your own security?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for building towers to make my own name great. Teach me to stop grasping and start receiving, finding my name and my security in Christ alone.
Amen.
